title: Latency degradation vs compression scenarios — regional GPU pool sizing (Jul 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Provide a working sensitivity sheet to estimate how different "compression" (precision reduction / quantization) and batching choices affect throughput, p95 latency, utilization, and expected quality degradation across regional GPU pools. This is intended to feed into Q3 capacity commits and Dedicated node sizing conversations.

Executive summary: 
- Aggressive compression (4-bit / LLM-adapted 4/bit kernels) with large batch sizes increases tokens/sec by 2.2–3.8x vs fp16 but can introduce measurable output-quality delta (~-4% to -8% on our eval set).
- For latency-sensitive workloads (p95 SLA < 300ms), prefer H100 + fp16 with small batches (1–4) and prefix caching; compression only in background/off-peak.
- For high-throughput, cost-sensitive workloads (background embedding/analysis pipelines), int8 + batch 16–32 is a good sweet spot (1.6–2.6x throughput, ~-1% to -3% quality).
- Regional recommendations: prioritize H100 capacity in us-west and europe-west for product-facing chat; allow more compressed configurations in apac-east and us-east for low-priority batch jobs.

Assumptions & metrics (definitions):
- Throughput: tokens_per_sec measured on canonical 512-token prompt load test.
- p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile end-to-end request latency measured with streaming disabled.
- util_pct: GPU utilization measured by our runtime accounting during steady-state QPS.
- quality_delta_pct: relative change in evaluation score (higher is better) computed on a 1k prompt eval set vs fp16 baseline; negative means degradation.
- projected_qps: number of 512-token-equivalent requests/sec the pool can sustain before util_pct > 85%.

Quick sanity checks (how numbers were derived):
- Base fp16 single-token throughput measured on microbench harness, scaled to 512 tokens.
- int8 and 4-bit multipliers derived from kernel benchmarks: int8 ~2.2x vs fp16 at mid batch sizes, 4-bit ~3.5x at large batches but with increased memory pressure and lower cache hitrates.
- p95 latency increases with batch_size roughly sublinearly; we apply an empirical model: p95 ~= p95_base * (1 + 0.025 * batch_size) + batch_overhead_ms. This roughly matches stress runs.
- quality deltas taken from our eval harness: smaller changes for int8 (-1% to -3%), larger for 4-bit (-4% to -8%) depending on model sensitivity.

Sensitivity notes (what changes most):
- Average prompt length: higher avg_tokens leads to lower projected_qps but similar tokens/sec; regional sizing must use realistic average token distributions.
- Cache hit rate: prefix/KV cache improves p95 significantly for chat workloads; scenarios above assume 40% cache hit for dialog-style prompts; with 70% hit, util_pct drops ~18% for fp16 small-batch scenarios.
- Model architecture: some decoder-only models degrade less under 4-bit quantization; always validate per-model.

Heatmap guidance (how to build):
- Create a 2D heatmap with x-axis = precision (fp16, int8, 4-bit) and y-axis = batch_size (1,2,4,8,16,32). Color = tokens_per_sec normalized by cost per hour. Overlay contour lines for quality_delta_pct thresholds (-1%, -3%, -5%).
- Use region-specific GPU types as separate sheets.

Recommendations / Target configurations: 
- Product chat (p95 SLA <= 300ms): H100 fp16 with batch <= 4; prefer H100 pools in us-west and europe-west.
- Throughput/ETL pipelines: A100 or H100 with int8, batch 8–16 depending on memory constraints.
- Cost-optimized analytics: 4-bit + batch 16–32 for off-peak jobs only; add layered validation to detect quality regressions early.

Action items (owners):
- Ethan Cole: run additional runs for S7 & S8 using the 2k prompt eval set (due 2026-07-27).
- Priya Raman: add heatmap sheet to the regional-capacity workbook and tag per-model sensitivity (due 2026-07-22).
- Sofia Martinez: prepare a short playbook for fallbacks when quantized pools exceed quality thresholds (draft due 2026-08-02).

Open questions / risks:
- We need clearer cost normalization across cloud vendors (spot vs committed GCP vs on-prem); current costs use GCP list prices.
- Some customer prompts contain long system instructions that reduce effective batch headroom — we need token distribution by customer segment.
- Kernel availability for 4-bit on older A100 drivers — confirm hardware+driver compatibility.

References and artifacts:
- linked_artifacts: CONFLUENCE-9876, JIRA-INF-2341 (see linked_artifacts header)
- Bench harness: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pool-compression-runs (internal)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working sheet; numbers are approximate and intended to be a starting point for committed capacity decisions. Please comment inline on any row that looks unrealistic for your workloads.
